stage_a.note: Clear positive engagement recurs alongside neutral stretches; he smiles when introducing the polo solution.
Sustained engagement with the subject and excitement about his product is evident across the presentation.
Friendly, approachable, and considerate expression characterizes much of his delivery from the opening.

venture.description: A polo shirt with a firm dress collar designed to be worn comfortably under a sweater or blazer.
venture.note: The founder is seeking $300,000 for 4% of his innovative apparel company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 presents his company Collars & Co, explaining the problem of uncomfortable dress shirts and his solution, a dress collar polo.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 hands out four different collar styles to the panel for them to examine.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 examines the shirt sample handed to him by the founder.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 comments on the nice stretchy material of the shirt sample.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the material is stretchy, lightweight, and breathable.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks the founder to confirm that he is offering four percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that he is offering four percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks what the company's sales have been so far.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they started last year and have sold 92,000 shirts for 5.4 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the sales are direct to consumer or through other channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that all sales are direct to consumer and online.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks what the profit margin was on those sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that the net profit margin is 20 percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 states he hates the midtown look and decides to exit the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 praises the company's fast growth, noting that reaching five million in sales makes it a real business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees with S5's assessment of the business.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 suggests the founder must have specific executional skills to achieve such fast growth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attributes the success to his marketing and funnel expertise, noting his 20 years of experience.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what specific work the founder has been doing for 20 years.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he has a background in business and internet marketing.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 states the business is not the right investment for her and exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 mentions his experience taking brands global and asks for the cost to make the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the landed cost is 15 dollars and it retails for 65 to 75 dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 notes the strong numbers and makes an offer of 300,000 dollars for 10 percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 deflects the offer by emphasizing the brand's fast growth rate and direct-to-consumer success.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 points out that the fast growth is exactly why S5 made the offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if the founder has any other investors in the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that he is the sole owner and has no other investors.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 criticizes the founder for dismissing S5's offer as if it were insignificant.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends his position, arguing the company is worth 20 million dollars, not the 3 million implied by the offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks the founder to justify why the company is worth 20 million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attempts to explain his valuation reasoning.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the company's free EBITDA.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the EBITDA is 20 percent, amounting to one million dollars on five million in sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what the founder intends to use the investment money for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the funds are needed for inventory, marketing, and building a team.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the founder plans to raise equity or get a line of credit for the inventory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they need a line of credit but are also looking for a mentor to help grow the business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 advises the founder to take the 10 percent offer in exchange for mentorship.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists that his company could become the next great brand.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 warns that the fashion market is brutal and trends shift rapidly, posing a risk.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 disagrees, stating he does not believe his product will go out of fashion.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 argues that a looming recession and inventory costs will hurt profits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends his product by comparing his core styles to established brands like Levi's.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 counters that even major brands like Levi's experience significant declines.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 states he is about to make an offer, noting his infrastructure can help cut costs and expand globally.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges S1's points.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 offers 300,000 dollars for 10 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 jokingly asks the other investors why they make offers when they know the founder will reject them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokes with S3 about expecting a smaller counter-offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 states the requested amount is insufficient and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reiterates the need for a 700,000 dollar line of credit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 re-enters, proposing to partner with S1 to offer 300,000 dollars for 10 percent plus a line of credit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues that their inventory represents hard assets, unlike tech apps.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 challenges the idea that clothing is a hard asset, calling it highly liquid.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 urges the founder to listen to S1 and S4, highlighting their extensive backgrounds.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the founder is preparing to make a counter-offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 criticizes the founder for wasting time and dismissing the investors' advice.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 complains that the investors are valuing his company at only 3 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 tells the founder to stop complaining and state his counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S4 and S1's offer, asking if they would accept 5 percent equity instead of 10.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 expresses disbelief at the founder's low counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 maintains that giving up 10 percent equity is too much.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 states that if 10 percent is too much, he is out, and withdraws his offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 tells the founder he has done well to receive a 10 percent offer given the business's value.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks S1 if he is suggesting the business is only worth half a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 clarifies he is referring to the incremental value they bring.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 complains that despite projecting 10 million in sales, the investors are valuing the company at 3 million.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 criticizes the founder for not listening, warning that this is a bad sign for a partnership.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 assures S1 that he is listening and understands his points.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 argues that the founder's behavior shows he is not listening and fails to grasp the opportunity's scale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists he is not discounting the value the investors bring, which is why he is there.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks the founder to consider the value if they help grow the company to 200 million.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 points out that partnering with S1 and S4 could realistically boost sales to 80 million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 reminds the founder that the investors have decades of experience and see many deals.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 bluntly states that the investors' lives will not change if the deal falls through.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 emphasizes that the founder could never afford to hire them as mentors without giving up equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 questions the founder's logic of wanting a discount while maintaining a 20 million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 expresses her feeling that the founder is not going to secure a deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 declares that he is out of the negotiation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters the previous offer by asking if S1 and S4 would accept 7 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 declines the counter-offer and confirms that he is out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reiterates that they are out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 warns the founder that he will likely regret walking away from the opportunity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 points out that the founder still has a chance to accept the standing offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 restates S4 and S1's offer of 300,000 dollars for 10 percent plus a line of credit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 confirms that he is still willing to do the deal under those terms.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 confirms his participation and demands a definitive yes or no from the founder.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts the offer from S4 and S1.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses satisfaction that the deal is closed.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 congratulates both the founder and the investors on reaching an agreement.

decisions.note: Hates the midtown look with all his heart.
While they are nice, it is not the right investment for her.
Never bid on a shirt deal but the numbers justify it.
Can take the product and sell it all over the world.
$300k is not enough and the founder already knows where to get capital.

decisions.note: Partnering with Peter, willing to put up the line of credit at 8-9%.

decisions.terms: $300,000 cash and $700,000 line of credit for 5%
decisions.note: Wants to lower the equity given up.
Founder thinks 10% is too much, so he drops out.
Frustrated that the founder is not listening and wants a discount.
Asks if they would do the deal for 7%.
Declines the 7% counter and goes out.
Confirms that they are all out.
Confirms he is still in on the original offer after Kevin restates it.
